objective: Decide whether a small repair shop has enough cash to take on a larger order.

sections.heading: Executive assessment
paragraphs: Ask for the bank balance and the first order’s cash schedule before committing to the job. The shop would have to buy parts before it collects from the customer.

sections.heading: Scope and input inventory
paragraphs: This fictional intake describes a repair shop with a proposed order. The example includes no bank statement, signed order or accounts.

sections.heading: Business and product
paragraphs: The owner describes a repair service that bills after completion. The customer’s price and payment date are unconfirmed.

sections.heading: Team
paragraphs: The intake identifies the owner but gives no staffing or subcontractor commitments.

sections.heading: Market and competition
paragraphs: No competing quotes or evidence of customer choice accompany the proposed order.

sections.heading: Independent thesis and reconciliation
paragraphs: The owner expects the order to pay for its parts. A parts deposit could fall due before the customer pays. A signed order and supplier terms would establish the sequence.

sections.heading: Financial analysis and calculations
paragraphs: Opening cash and the cost of materials are unknown. A cash shortfall or runway cannot be calculated.

sections.heading: Material factors and evidence coverage
paragraphs: The two facts most likely to change the decision are the unrestricted balance and the deposit required to order parts.

sections.heading: Risks and safeguards
paragraphs: If the customer cancels after parts are bought, the shop may have to fund the deposit from its own cash. Cancellation terms are missing.

sections.heading: Valuation and sensitivity
paragraphs: Not estimable. The intake contains no earnings history, cash-flow forecast or comparable transaction.

sections.heading: Management questions
paragraphs: What deposit does the supplier require, when is the customer obliged to pay, and how much unrestricted cash is available on the deposit date?

sections.heading: Methodology and limitations
paragraphs: Only the fictional intake was reviewed. All order terms remain management representations.

sources.title: Fictional owner intake
sources.locator: Owner’s description of the proposed order, 27 November 2026

missing_information.item: Bank reconciliation, customer order and supplier deposit terms
missing_information.period: At order acceptance and each payment date through collection
missing_information.why: Parts may be payable before the customer settles the invoice.
missing_information.conclusion: Whether the shop can take the order without short-term borrowing.
missing_information.action: Lay out the deposit and collection dates against unrestricted cash.
